bugClass.title: Canary verdict rejects valid answers from client-specific actors
bugClass.cause: A verdict or acceptance check compares an actor field against one hard-coded identity even though different client write paths record different actor strings or omit the field and rely on a default. Test fakes that omit actor metadata can conceal the mismatch.
bugClass.criteria: Classify another site when a verdict or acceptance check requires an exact actor identity and at least one valid client path writes a different identity or leaves it unset for a default. Separate client paths are sufficient independently. Include cases where test doubles omit or normalize actor metadata and therefore fail to represent production writes.

candidates.evidence: `surfaceAnswerers` explicitly lists valid write identities by client: web `'Daniel via Hub'`, Mac `'daniel'`, and iPhone `'Daniel'` (lines 1–11). This establishes the actor mismatch across client paths; the iPhone path records a different identity from the other two. The excerpt does not show the verdict comparison itself, so it does not establish a rejection trigger at this site.

`awaitTap` reads an answer and passes it to `judgeAnswer` (lines 44–56), but the excerpt does not show whether that verdict compares `answered_by` with a literal or accepts the client-specific actors. The trigger and any limiting guard cannot be established here.

The Mac row-choice test checks only that answered_by is truthy after a tap (lines 32–44). It does not show the production actor written by this path or an exact-identity verdict check, so the mismatch mechanism is not established.

The test support records `Daniel via Hub` for web and `Daniel` for iPhone, while `tapAsk` writes the app-specific value or a supplied `by` override (lines 56–66). This shows differing actor strings in the test world, but the excerpt does not show a verdict or acceptance check requiring an exact identity.
`TrackerItemDetailFields` includes `answered_by` (line 64), but this type excerpt contains no verdict or acceptance check and shows no client write paths or actor comparison.
`answered_by` is included in the `textFields` set (line 33), indicating normalization as a text field. The excerpt shows no exact actor check or client-specific writes.
